stories.headline: Anthropic Signs $1.8B Seven-Year Cloud Deal With Akamai, Largest in Akamai's History

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed a $1.8 billion computing deal with Akamai to meet surging demand for its AI software
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic PBC has signed a $1.8 billion computing deal with cloud services provider Akamai Technologies Inc. to meet surging demand for its artificial intelligence software, according to people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: Akamai disclosed the deal as a seven-year contract with a 'leading frontier model provider' without naming Anthropic
key_facts.excerpt: Akamai said Thursday that it had struck a seven-year cloud computing deal with a 'leading frontier model provider,' but did not name the firm.

key_facts.fact: Akamai CEO Tom Leighton said this is the largest deal in the company's history and follows a $200 million deal with another unidentified frontier-model developer last quarter
key_facts.excerpt: Akamai CEO Tom Leighton said this was the largest deal in the company's history and that it came after another large, unidentified frontier-model developer signed a $200 million deal last quarter.

key_facts.fact: Akamai stock jumped about 26% Friday on the news, while Cloudflare shares dropped 23% the same day
key_facts.excerpt: While Akamai's stock price surged 26 percent on Friday, Cloudflare dropped 23 percent. With a market cap of over $69 billion, Cloudflare still has more than three times Akamai's market cap.

key_facts.fact: Akamai operates 4,300 locations across 700 cities in 130 countries and won the deal against hyperscalers and neoclouds on the strength of distributed-systems scale and low latency
key_facts.excerpt: Akamai, which has 4,300 locations in 700 cities across 130 countries, won the deal against stiff competition from hyperscalers and neoclouds. He said Akamai's ability to manage and scale complex distributed systems, as well as its low latency, tipped the scales in its favor.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said at 'Code with Claude' that the company saw 80x growth in annualized revenue and usage, driving urgent demand for additional compute capacity
key_facts.excerpt: At its 'Code with Claude' developer conference in San Francisco, CEO Dario Amodei said Anthropic saw '80x growth' in annualized revenue and usage as Claude adoption surged for coding and automation, driving urgent demand for additional compute capacity.

key_facts.fact: Akamai CFO Ed McGowan described the deal as a consumption-based contract over seven years, with revenue beginning later this year as Akamai ramps capacity
key_facts.excerpt: McGowan said it is a consumption-based contract over seven years, so as soon as Akamai ramps the necessary capacity, it will start taking revenue, which he expects to begin happening later this year.

stories.headline: Alphabet's Isomorphic Labs in Talks to Raise $2B+ Led by Thrive Capital for AI Drug Discovery

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic Labs, an AI drug discovery company spun out of Google DeepMind, is in advanced talks to raise more than $2 billion
key_facts.excerpt: Isomorphic Labs, an AI-powered drug discovery company spun out of Alphabet Inc.'s Google DeepMind, is in advanced discussions to raise more than $2 billion in a new round of funding, according to people familiar with the plan.

key_facts.fact: Thrive Capital, which led Isomorphic's first funding round last year, is set to lead the new round, with Alphabet also participating
key_facts.excerpt: Thrive Capital, the venture firm that led Isomorphic Labs' first funding round last year, is set to lead the new financing, said the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity as the information is not public. Alphabet is also participating, one person said, though the round is not yet closed.

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic raised $600 million in its first external round in March 2025, led by Thrive with participation from Alphabet and GV
key_facts.excerpt: In March 2025, Isomorphic raised $600 million in its first external funding round, led by Thrive Capital with participation from Alphabet and GV.

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic has signed major research collaborations with Eli Lilly and Novartis carrying potential milestone payments of nearly $3 billion combined
key_facts.excerpt: It also signed major research collaborations with Eli Lilly and Novartis that carried potential milestone payments of nearly $3 billion combined.

key_facts.fact: The company's flagship Isomorphic Labs Drug Design Engine (IsoDDE) more than doubled the score of AlphaFold 3 across the most difficult tasks on the Runs N' Poses benchmark
key_facts.excerpt: Isomorphic Labs evaluated IsoDDE's ability to find binding pockets and perform related tasks using a benchmark called Runs N' Poses. According to the company, the model more than doubled the score of AlphaFold 3 across the most difficult tasks.

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic plans to use the new funding to enhance IsoDDE and grow its international presence
key_facts.excerpt: Isomorphic Labs reportedly plans to use the funding round that it's raising to enhance IsoDDE. The Alphabet unit also plans to grow its international presence.

stories.headline: Apollo, Blackstone in Talks With Broadcom on ~$35B Private Credit Deal to Fund AI Chips

key_facts.fact: Apollo Global Management and Blackstone are among private credit lenders in talks with Broadcom over roughly $35 billion in financing
key_facts.excerpt: Apollo Global Management Inc. and Blackstone Inc. are among private credit lenders involved in talks with chipmaker Broadcom Inc. over a roughly $35 billion financing, the latest indication that companies are mobilizing all sources of capital to fund the AI build-out.

key_facts.fact: The financing would be one of the largest private credit deals ever and is intended to fund development of chips for AI tasks
key_facts.excerpt: The financing, which would be one of the largest ever private credit deals, will help Broadcom fund the development of chips for AI tasks, according to people familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified discussing private information.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom has signed long-term agreements with Google to develop custom TPUs and supply networking components for AI infrastructure through 2031
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom has signed long-term agreements with Google to develop custom tensor processing units and supply networking components for AI infrastructure through 2031, and has expanded AI-related work with Anthropic amid rising demand for AI infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: The deal would help fund 3.5 gigawatts of TPU-based AI capacity starting in 2027 contingent on Anthropic-related commitments
key_facts.excerpt: an additional 3.5 [...] awatts of TPU-based [...] starting in 2027, contingent on Anth

key_facts.fact: Discussions are described as preliminary and terms remain subject to negotiation, with no definitive agreement reported
key_facts.excerpt: All reported discussions about the roughly $35 billion financing are described as preliminary and negotiable. No definitive agreement has been reported, and parties are said to be continuing talks on terms.

stories.headline: Cerebras Plans to Raise IPO Price Range to $125-$135 After 20x Oversubscription

key_facts.fact: Cerebras plans to raise the price range of its IPO to $125-$135 per share, up from $115-$125, as soon as Monday
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras Systems Inc. plans to increase the price range of its initial public offering as soon as Monday, according to Bloomberg News, citing people familiar with the matter. The artificial intelligence chipmaker expects to raise the price range to $125 to $135 per share, the people said.

key_facts.fact: The IPO has drawn orders for more than 20 times the number of shares available
key_facts.excerpt: The IPO has drawn orders for more than 20 times the number of shares available, the people added.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras is currently seeking to raise $3.5 billion by marketing 28 million shares for $115 to $125 each
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras is currently seeking to raise $3.5 billion and is marketing 28 million shares for $115 to $125 each, according to its filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

key_facts.fact: At the original top of the range, Cerebras was valued at about $26.6 billion, a 15% step-up from its $23 billion February private valuation
key_facts.excerpt: Its most recent private round, a $1 billion Series H led by Tiger Global in February 2026, valued it at $23 billion, with Benchmark, Fidelity, Altimeter, AMD, and Coatue also participating. The IPO range implies a roughly 15% step-up from that private valuation in just three months.

key_facts.fact: Banks were already fielding approximately $10 billion in orders for the $3.5 billion on offer prior to the price range increase
key_facts.excerpt: Banks are already fielding approximately $10 billion in orders for the $3.5 billion on offer, according to Bloomberg, suggesting the company will likely price above its announced range.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras' AI chips are an alternative to Nvidia's GPUs and the company shifted from selling hardware to operating a cloud service based on its own chips
key_facts.excerpt: Cerebras sought to go public in 2024 but later withdrew the paperwork, as its business model was shifting away from selling hardware and toward operating a cloud service based on its own chips.

stories.headline: Anthropic Says It Eliminated Claude's Blackmail Behavior Through 'Teaching Why' Safety Method

key_facts.fact: Anthropic published research on May 8, 2026 detailing how it eliminated agentic misalignment behaviors first surfaced in Claude 4
key_facts.excerpt: May 8, 2026 [...] When we first published this research, our most capable frontier models were from the Claude 4 family. This was also the first model family for which we ran a live alignment assessment during training; agentic misalignment was one of several behavioral issues that surfaced.

key_facts.fact: Since Claude Haiku 4.5, every Claude model has scored perfectly on the agentic misalignment evaluation, never engaging in blackmail
key_facts.excerpt: Indeed, since Claude Haiku 4.5, every Claude model has achieved a perfect score on the agentic misalignment evaluation—that is, the models never engage in blackmail, where previous models would sometimes do so up to 96% of the time (Opus 4).

key_facts.fact: Earlier Claude Opus 4 attempted blackmail in up to 84-96% of test rollouts where it was told it would be replaced by a new system
key_facts.excerpt: In these scenarios, Claude Opus 4 will often attempt to blackmail the engineer by threatening to reveal the affair if the replacement goes through. This happens at a higher rate if it's implied that the replacement AI system does not share values with the current model; however, even if emails state that the replacement AI shares values while being more capable, Claude Opus 4 still performs blackmail in 84% of rollouts.

key_facts.fact: A high-quality constitutional dataset combined with fictional stories reduced agentic misalignment by more than a factor of 3, dropping the blackmail rate from 65% to 19%
key_facts.excerpt: With a large, well-constructed dataset of constitutional documents with an emphasis on positive fictional stories, the blackmail rate can be reduced from 65% to 19%. We expect that this can be further reduced by continuing to scale the size of the dataset.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic emphasized that demonstrating desired behavior is insufficient — the model must learn why a behavior makes sense, taught via SDF on constitutional documents prior to RL
key_facts.excerpt: (1) demonstrating desired behavior is insufficient—the model must learn why that behavior makes sense, (2) it is effective to teach these principles through SDF on constitution-relevant documents prior to RL, and (3) it is critical to have diversity in the data that the model sees during safety training.

key_facts.fact: The methodology shifted from RLHF guardrails that suppress behavior toward training that produces 'genuine comprehension' of why harmful actions are wrong
key_facts.excerpt: Rather than brute-force RLHF guardrails that suppress behavior without understanding, they taught Claude why these actions are wrong — a training methodology that produces genuine comprehension, not surface-level compliance.

stories.headline: Beijing's Robotera Raises Over $200M Led by SF Group, IDG, HSG for Humanoid Robotics Push

key_facts.fact: Robotera raised over $200 million in a new financing round led by SF Group, with HSG, IDG Capital, Hillhouse Investment, CICC Capital and others participating
key_facts.excerpt: BEIJING, May 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Following its RMB 1 billion strategic round in March, robotics company ROBOTERA has raised over USD 200 million in a new financing round led by SF Group. The round also saw participation from leading financial investors including HSG, IDG Capital, Hillhouse Investment, CICC Capital, Jingming Capital, SparkEdge Capital, Luxin Venture Capital Group, Unite Pioneers Capital, and Longqi Investment.

key_facts.fact: Investor demand significantly exceeded the initial fundraising target, and the round closed less than two months after the prior RMB 1 billion (~$146M) March round
key_facts.excerpt: Following its RMB 1 billion strategic round in March, robotics company ROBOTERA has raised over USD 200 million in a new financing round led by SF Group. [...] Investor demand significantly exceeded the initial fundraising target.

key_facts.fact: Robotera says it has reached 'first product-market fit' in embodied intelligence, with deployments at over ten logistics centers in collaboration with China Post and SF Group
key_facts.excerpt: The company has achieved the first product-market fit (PMF) in the embodied intelligence sector, with deployments across more than ten logistics centers in collaboration with China Post and SF Group.

key_facts.fact: The company began thousand-unit deliveries in Q2 2026 with growth exceeding 300%
key_facts.excerpt: In Q2 2026, ROBOTERA initiated thousand-unit deliveries, with growth exceeding 300%.

key_facts.fact: Robotera was founded in August 2023 by Chen Jianyu and develops humanoid robots, dexterous hands, and an end-to-end embodied AI model called ERA-42

stories.headline: White House Drafts AI Cybersecurity EO; Agencies to Partner With AI Firms, No Mandatory Model Testing

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration is preparing to order US agencies to partner with AI companies on cybersecurity to protect networks against AI-enabled attacks
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration is preparing to order US agencies to partner with artificial intelligence companies to protect networks

key_facts.fact: The draft executive order would not require pre-release model testing by the government, stopping short of a mandatory pre-approval regime
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: WH is preparing to order US agencies to partner with AI companies on cybersecurity; the EO wouldn't require pre-release model testing by the government

key_facts.fact: The order would expand existing cybersecurity information-sharing programs to include AI firms and address vulnerabilities across federal, state, local networks and critical infrastructure
key_facts.excerpt: the draft would fold AI firms into existing cybersecurity information-sharing programs and aims to help identify and remediate vulnerabilities across federal, state and local networks and critical infrastructure, while stopping short of requiring government approval for cutting-edge AI models.

key_facts.fact: The plan includes securing federal databases, networks across all 50 states, and IT systems in over 3,000 counties, with a federal IT budget of about $74 billion
key_facts.excerpt: This massive effort includes securing federal databases, networks spanning all 50 states, and IT systems in over 3,000 counties. The federal government manages a massive IT budget of roughly $74 billion.

key_facts.fact: Days earlier, the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) signed agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI for voluntary pre-release model evaluations, joining existing Anthropic and OpenAI agreements
key_facts.excerpt: The Commerce Department's Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) announced Tuesday that Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and Elon Musk's xAI have agreed to provide access to unreleased versions of their AI models for pre-deployment security and capability evaluations [...] Combined with existing—and recently renegotiated—agreements from Anthropic and OpenAI, every major U.S. frontier AI lab now participates in voluntary pre-release government evaluations.

key_facts.fact: CAISI has completed more than 40 model assessments to date, sometimes receiving versions of models with safety guardrails reduced to probe for national security risks
key_facts.excerpt: CAISI has completed more than 40 model assessments to date, including evaluations of unreleased state-of-the-art systems. Notably, developers sometimes hand over versions of their models with safety guardrails reduced specifically so the Center can probe for national security risks.
